Package com.j3d.gen.settings

Class Setting<T>

java.lang.Object
com.j3d.gen.settings.Setting<T>
Type Parameters:
T - The type of the setting.
All Implemented Interfaces:
EventEmitterInterface, SettingsChild
Direct Known Subclasses:
BooleanSetting, ComplexSetting, DoubleSetting, EnumSetting, IntSetting, StringSetting
public class Setting<T> extends Object implements SettingsChild, EventEmitterInterface
A generic class representing a single setting.

This class is used to store a single setting, along with its description. It can be used for any type of setting, by specifying the type parameter <T>.

A setting also serializes into a key value pair. (although this is usually with dot syntax) So the setting CameraProperties.movementSpeed serializes into: 


     settings.cameraProperties.movementSpeed = 5.0
and alot more logic that's readable in serialize() deserialize(ArrayList) provided by SettingsChild and also found in SettingsParent

Author:
Lehlogonolo Poole

    • serialize

      public ArrayList<String> serialize()
      Serializes the current setting into a list of strings. For a single setting, this typically returns a list containing one string in the format "settingName = settingValue".
      Specified by:
      serialize in interface SettingsChild
      Returns:
      An ArrayList of strings representing the serialized setting.

    • deserialize

      public void deserialize(ArrayList<String> leftover)
      Deserializes the setting's value from a list of strings. It searches for a string containing the serialized name of this setting, parses its value, and updates the setting. If no match is found or parsing fails, the setting is reset to its default value.
      Specified by:
      deserialize in interface SettingsChild
      Parameters:
      leftover - An ArrayList of strings from which to deserialize the setting.
